prompt: A colony of $100$ cells doubles every $3$ hours. How many cells are there after $12$ hours?
hint: The clock is in hours, but the growth happens in DOUBLINGS. Count the doublings first.

hints.text: The clock is in hours, but the growth happens in DOUBLINGS. Count the doublings first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: something doubling every $2$ hours for $6$ hours doubles $6 \div 2 = 3$ times. Same move — divide the total time by the doubling time.
The number of doublings is $12 \div 3 = 4$. Each one multiplies by $2$, so work out $100 \cdot 2^4$.
Since $2^4 = 16$, there are $100 \times 16 = 1600$ cells after $12$ hours.

explanation: The doubling time is $3$ hours, so $12$ hours holds $12 \div 3 = 4$ doublings.
Each doubling multiplies the count by $2$, so four of them multiply it by $2^4 = 16$.
Starting from $100$ cells, that gives $100 \times 16 = 1600$ cells.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk the clock
steps: Only the doubling moments matter, not every single hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write the formula first
steps: With doubling time $3$, the rule is $y = 100 \cdot 2^{t/3}$.
